questions.question: When you slow down or stop, you should:

options.text: Take the bike out of gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift down through the gears.
questions.explanation: Shift down through the gears using the clutch as you slow or stop. Stay in first gear while stopped so you can move quickly if needed.

questions.question: Signals on a motorcycle:

options.text: Are even more important than signals on cars and trucks.
Should only be used when another vehicle is right next to you.
Are less important than signals on cars and trucks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are even more important than signals on cars and trucks.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle riders are more vulnerable than car and truck drivers. That is why using signals correctly is even more important for motorcyclists.

questions.question: If bright sunlight makes it hard for drivers to see your turn signals, you should:

options.text: Continue to use the mechanical turn signals.
Honk your horn to tell other drivers about upcoming turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use hand signals.
questions.explanation: Use hand signals when bright sunlight makes your turn signals hard to see. It is very important to communicate clearly with other drivers.

questions.question: If you cannot avoid a slippery road, you should:

options.text: Lean into the slippery section to keep your balance.
Keep your speed the same to stay on the road.
Not worry about the road conditions.
Keep your motorcycle upright and go as slowly as needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your motorcycle upright and go as slowly as needed.
questions.explanation: The best choice is to avoid slippery roads. If you cannot avoid a slippery area, keep your motorcycle upright and go as slowly as possible.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT protective clothing for a motorcyclist?
questions.correctAnswerText: A stocking cap
questions.explanation: Wear protective clothing when riding. This includes sturdy pants and jackets that cover your arms and legs, boots or heavy shoes that cover your ankles, and sturdy gloves. A stocking cap is not protective gear.

questions.question: When the lights on this sign are flashing, what should you do?

options.text: Stop and wait until the train passes.
Turn around and find another route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and wait until the train passes.
questions.explanation: When you see flashing lights at a railroad crossing, you must stop completely and wait until the train passes and the lights stop flashing. Never try to beat a train across the tracks.

questions.question: Check that your headlight and taillight work:
questions.correctAnswerText: Before every ride.
questions.explanation: Always test your lights before you ride. Working lights are essential to your safety every time you are on the road.

questions.question: Snow and ice melt:

options.text: Only when the sun hits them directly.
At the same speed on all roads.
Most quickly on bridges and overpasses.
Faster on some parts of the road than others.

questions.correctAnswerText: Faster on some parts of the road than others.
questions.explanation: Snow and ice melt at different speeds in different places. Low areas, shaded areas, bridges, and overpasses stay frozen the longest.

questions.question: Reflective, brightly-colored helmets and clothing:

options.text: Should only be worn when riding at night.
Help other drivers see you better.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help other drivers see you better.
questions.explanation: Wearing brightly-colored or reflective clothing makes it easier for other drivers to see you on the road.

questions.question: A sign that your rear tire has gone flat is:

options.text: The back of your motorcycle is swaying side to side.

questions.correctAnswerText: The back of your motorcycle is swaying side to side.
questions.explanation: If your rear tire goes flat, the back of your motorcycle may jerk or sway side to side. If you feel this movement, stop riding and check your tires as soon as possible.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Vehicles will be entering the roadway.
Stop completely. Then go when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely. Then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: Red octagonal signs are always stop signs. You must stop completely, check for other traffic and pedestrians, and then go when it is safe.

questions.question: If another driver is following you too closely, what should you do?

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle tailgating is to get the other driver ahead of you. If it is safe, change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up may only make them tailgate you faster.

questions.question: Can you ride around lowered gates at a railroad crossing?

options.text: Yes, when the lights stop flashing.
Yes, when other drivers do it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: You must stop at any railroad crossing when warning signals appear. These include flashing red lights, lowered gates, a flagger, or a train whistle. Going around a lowered gate is illegal.

questions.question: Why should you wear riding gloves?

options.text: You should not wear them because they make your hands too hot.
They give you a better grip on the handlebars.
You should not wear them because they make controls harder to use.
Wear them only on cool days.

questions.correctAnswerText: They give you a better grip on the handlebars.
questions.explanation: Wear leather or durable gloves when riding. They improve your grip on the handlebars and protect your hands if you crash.

questions.question: Before riding, check the throttle. What should it do when you release it?
questions.correctAnswerText: Snap back.
questions.explanation: Before riding, check your clutch and throttle. The throttle should snap back when you release it. The clutch should feel tight and smooth.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slow down. Stop if cars are near.
Stop completely. Then go when it is safe.
Go carefully through the intersection without always stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely. Then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: An octagonal sign always means stop. Stop at the marked line. If there is no line, stop before the crosswalk. If there is no crosswalk, stop where you can see oncoming traffic. Go only when it is safe.

questions.question: What should your lane position do?

options.text: Hide your plans from other drivers.
Encourage other drivers to share your lane.
Help you see and be seen better.
Keep you close to road signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help you see and be seen better.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see others and lets them see you. It helps you avoid wind blasts, blind spots, and road hazards. It discourages other drivers from sharing your lane and gives you an escape route if needed.

questions.question: What best reduces the risk of head or neck injury in a crash?
questions.correctAnswerText: Wearing a helmet.
questions.explanation: Wearing a helmet is the single best way to reduce head and neck injuries in a crash.

questions.question: Downshifting to a lower gear is also called:
questions.correctAnswerText: Engine braking.
questions.explanation: Shifting to a lower gear works like using brakes. This is why downshifting is called engine braking.

questions.question: How can you reduce your chance of an accident?

options.text: Do not look ahead for hazards.
Do not use turn signals because they distract other drivers.
Make sure other drivers can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure other drivers can see you.
questions.explanation: To avoid crashes, be visible to others, signal your moves clearly, keep safe distance, watch the road ahead, and spot hazards early. Always be ready to react.

questions.question: Taking a turn too fast can cause a rider to:

options.text: Drift into another lane of traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drift into another lane of traffic.
questions.explanation: Taking a turn too fast can cause you to cross into another lane or leave the road. Always slow down before turning.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Construction and maintenance warning signs.
questions.explanation: Orange signs are used only for construction and maintenance warnings.

questions.question: When slowing or stopping a motorcycle, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Shift down through the gears.
questions.explanation: Shift down through the gears as you slow or stop. Stay in first gear when stopped so you can move quickly if needed.

questions.question: Unlike other beverages, alcohol:
questions.correctAnswerText: Enters the bloodstream immediately.
questions.explanation: Alcohol does not need to be digested. It is absorbed directly through the stomach and small intestine into the bloodstream and quickly reaches the brain.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: School zone ahead
questions.explanation: Pentagonal signs warn you that you are in or approaching a school zone or school crossing. Watch for children and follow posted speed limits.

questions.question: When slowing down or stopping, you must:
questions.correctAnswerText: Shift down through the gears.
questions.explanation: Shift down through the gears as you slow down or stop. Stay in first gear when stopped so you can move quickly if needed.

questions.question: You may carry a passenger:

options.text: Only if the passenger is a child.
Only if the passenger has a motorcycle license.
If the motorcycle is equipped to carry a passenger.

questions.correctAnswerText: If the motorcycle is equipped to carry a passenger.
questions.explanation: You can only carry a passenger if your motorcycle is designed and equipped for a passenger.

questions.question: The front brake is:

options.text: Only for use if the rear brake fails.

questions.correctAnswerText: Safe if used properly.
questions.explanation: The front brake is safe when used correctly. It is more powerful than the rear brake and provides at least three-fourths of your stopping power.

questions.question: What can remove alcohol from a person's system?
questions.correctAnswerText: Time
questions.explanation: Only time can remove alcohol from your body. Nothing else can speed up this process.

questions.question: A DOT-compliant helmet has all of the following, except:

options.text: Bright colors painted on the outside.

questions.correctAnswerText: Bright colors painted on the outside.
questions.explanation: A DOT-compliant helmet must have an impact-resistant outer shell, an impact-absorbing inner liner, a comfort liner, and a chinstrap retention system. Bright colors are not required.
